निम्नलिखित अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) पर विचार कीजिए।
अभिकथन (A): अल्पसंख्यक शैक्षणिक संस्थान अपनी अल्पसंख्यक पहचान बनाए रखने के लिए अपनी सीटों में से 50 प्रतिशत तक अपने समुदाय के विद्यार्थियों के लिए आरक्षित कर सकता है।
कारण (R): सेंट स्टीफेंस कॉलेज मामले में सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने माना कि सहायता प्राप्त अल्पसंख्यक संस्थान शेष सीटों को योग्यता के आधार पर भरते हुए अपने समुदाय के विद्यार्थियों को प्रवेश में प्राथमिकता दे सकते हैं।

questions.question_english:
Consider the following Assertion (A) and Reason (R).
Assertion (A): A minority educational institution can reserve up to 50% of its seats for students belonging to its own community.
Reason (R): The Supreme Court in the St. Stephen’s College case held that minority institutions can reserve seats for their community to maintain their minority character, provided the remaining seats are filled on merit.
options_english: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation_english: In St. Stephen's College v. University of Delhi (1992), the Supreme Court ruled that state-aided minority educational institutions can reserve up to 50% of seats for candidates from their own community to preserve their minority character, provided remaining seats are made available to other candidates on merit.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर है: A और R दोनों सही हैं तथा R, A की सही व्याख्या है। सेंट स्टीफेंस कॉलेज बनाम दिल्ली विश्वविद्यालय (1992) मामले में सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने सहायता प्राप्त अल्पसंख्यक संस्थानों के लिए अल्पसंख्यक समुदाय के विद्यार्थियों को प्रवेश में प्राथमिकता देने की अनुमति को मान्यता दी, साथ ही शेष सीटों पर योग्यता का महत्त्व बरकरार रखा। प्रश्न में उल्लिखित 50 प्रतिशत की सीमा स्रोत में वर्णित सिद्धांत के अनुरूप है; इसे सभी प्रकार के संस्थानों पर लागू सार्वभौमिक नियम न समझें।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: In St. Stephen's College v. University of Delhi (1992), the Supreme Court ruled that state-aided minority educational institutions can reserve up to 50% of seats for candidates from their own community to preserve their minority character, provided remaining seats are made available to other candidates on merit.

questions.question_english:
Consider the following Assertion (A) and Reason (R).
Assertion (A): The Right to Education under Article 21A applies equally to a 10-year-old child of a foreign national residing in India.
Reason (R): Fundamental Rights under Article 21 and Article 21A are available to all persons within the territory of India, not just citizens.
options_english: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation_english: Fundamental Rights under Article 21 (Life and Personal Liberty) and Article 21A (Right to Education) are guaranteed to all "persons" residing within the territory of India, unlike rights restricted strictly to "citizens" (such as Article 15, 16, 19, 29). Therefore, foreign children living in India possess the equal constitutional right to elementary education.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर A है। अनुच्छेद 21 जीवन और व्यक्तिगत स्वतंत्रता का अधिकार सभी व्यक्तियों को देता है, केवल भारतीय नागरिकों को नहीं। अनुच्छेद 21क भी 6 से 14 वर्ष की आयु के बच्चों के लिए शिक्षा का अधिकार व्यक्तियों को उपलब्ध कराता है। इसलिए भारत में रहने वाले विदेशी नागरिक का पात्र आयु-वर्ग का बच्चा भी इस अधिकार के दायरे में आता है, और कारण अभिकथन को स्पष्ट करता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Fundamental Rights under Article 21 (Life and Personal Liberty) and Article 21A (Right to Education) are guaranteed to all "persons" residing within the territory of India, unlike rights restricted strictly to "citizens" (such as Article 15, 16, 19, 29). Therefore, foreign children living in India possess the equal constitutional right to elementary education.

options_hindi: हाँ। अनुच्छेद 21क भारत में सभी बच्चों पर लागू होता है, चाहे उनकी नागरिकता की स्थिति कुछ भी हो।
नहीं। भाग III के सभी मौलिक अधिकार केवल प्रमाणित भारतीय नागरिकों को प्राप्त हैं।
हाँ, लेकिन बच्चे को विदेशी नागरिकों के लिए लागू पूरी गैर-सब्सिडी वाली फीस देनी होगी।
नहीं। RTE अधिनियम गैर-नागरिक बच्चों को राज्य द्वारा निःशुल्क शिक्षा दिए जाने से स्पष्ट रूप से बाहर रखता है।

questions.question_english: A Principal discovers that a newly admitted student's parents are undocumented immigrants. Under the ambit of Article 21A, does the child have the Right to Free and Compulsory Education?
options_english: Yes, Article 21A applies to all children within India, regardless of citizenship status.
No, because all Fundamental Rights under Part III of the Constitution are reserved exclusively for verified Indian citizens.
Yes, but the student can only be admitted if the parents pay full non-subsidized tuition fees applicable to foreign nationals.

questions.explanation_english: Article 21A guarantees the fundamental right to free and compulsory education to "all children" aged six to fourteen years residing within the territory of India. Unlike provisions restricted strictly to citizens, Article 21A covers every child present in India, regardless of their parents' legal citizenship or immigration status.
questions.explanation_hindi: स्रोत के अनुसार सही उत्तर है: हाँ, अनुच्छेद 21क भारत में सभी बच्चों पर लागू होता है, चाहे उनकी नागरिकता की स्थिति कुछ भी हो। अनुच्छेद 21क छह से चौदह वर्ष के सभी बच्चों के लिए निःशुल्क और अनिवार्य शिक्षा का अधिकार बताता है; इसका पाठ केवल नागरिक बच्चों तक सीमित शब्दावली का उपयोग नहीं करता। इसलिए माता-पिता की दस्तावेजी स्थिति के कारण बच्चे को स्वतः वंचित करना उचित नहीं होगा। विद्यालय को लागू RTE प्रावधानों और प्रशासनिक दिशा-निर्देशों के अनुरूप प्रवेश प्रक्रिया पूरी करनी चाहिए।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Yes, Article 21A applies to all children within India, regardless of citizenship status.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Article 21A guarantees the fundamental right to free and compulsory education to "all children" aged six to fourteen years residing within the territory of India. Unlike provisions restricted strictly to citizens, Article 21A covers every child present in India, regardless of their parents' legal citizenship or immigration status.

questions.question_english: Read the situation below and answer the question that follows: A recognized private school receiving financial aid from the Government of NCT of Delhi denies admission to a student on the grounds that the student does not belong to the religious denomination that founded the school. Which constitutional provision is being explicitly violated by the school's action?
options_english: Article 30(1)
Article 15(4)
Article 28(3)
Article 29(2)
questions.explanation_english: Article 29(2) explicitly provides that no citizen shall be denied admission into any educational institution maintained by the State or receiving aid out of State funds on grounds only of religion, race, caste, language, or any of them. Denying admission in an aided private school on religious grounds violates this fundamental nondiscrimination guarantee applicable to stateassisted educational facilities.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर अनुच्छेद 29(2) है। यह प्रावधान कहता है कि राज्य द्वारा संचालित या राज्य निधि से सहायता प्राप्त किसी शैक्षणिक संस्थान में किसी नागरिक को केवल धर्म, मूलवंश, जाति या भाषा के आधार पर प्रवेश से वंचित नहीं किया जा सकता। चूँकि विद्यालय सरकारी सहायता प्राप्त करता है, इसलिए वह इस संवैधानिक गैर-भेदभाव नियम से बँधा है। अल्पसंख्यक संस्था का दर्जा इस रोक को स्वतः समाप्त नहीं करता।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) Article 29(2)

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Article 29(2) explicitly provides that no citizen shall be denied admission into any educational institution maintained by the State or receiving aid out of State funds on grounds only of religion, race, caste, language, or any of them. Denying admission in an aided private school on religious grounds violates this fundamental nondiscrimination guarantee applicable to stateassisted educational facilities.

questions.question_english: Article 15(4) of the Constitution, which enables the State to make special provisions for the advancement of any socially and educationally backward classes of citizens, was added by which Constitutional Amendment?
options_english: 1st Amendment Act, 1951
4th Amendment Act, 1955

questions.explanation_english: Article 15(4) was added by the First Constitutional Amendment Act in 1951 following the Supreme Court judgment in Champakam Dorairajan. This amendment empowered the State to make special provisions for the educational advancement of socially and educationally backward classes of citizens, as well as Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर प्रथम संशोधन अधिनियम, 1951 है। अनुच्छेद 15(4) को चंपकम दोरैराजन मामले के बाद जोड़ा गया, ताकि राज्य सामाजिक और शैक्षणिक रूप से पिछड़े वर्गों तथा अनुसूचित जातियों और अनुसूचित जनजातियों की उन्नति के लिए विशेष प्रावधान कर सके। यह प्रावधान समानता के सिद्धांत के साथ सकारात्मक कार्रवाई को संवैधानिक आधार देता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) 1st Amendment Act, 1951

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Article 15(4) was added by the First Constitutional Amendment Act in 1951 following the Supreme Court judgment in Champakam Dorairajan. This amendment empowered the State to make special provisions for the educational advancement of socially and educationally backward classes of citizens, as well as Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

Consider these statements regarding the constitutional validity of the Right to Education Act:
I. The Supreme Court upheld the constitutional validity of the RTE Act in the Society for Unaided Private Schools of Rajasthan case.
II. The Court held that the 25% reservation in private unaided non-minority schools is a reasonable restriction under Article 19(6).

options_english: I and II
I and III
II and III

questions.explanation_english: In Society for Unaided Private Schools of Rajasthan (2012), the Supreme Court upheld the RTE Act and validated 25% reservations in private non-minority schools as reasonable restrictions under Article 19(6). questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर है: I और II। सोसायटी फॉर अनएडेड प्राइवेट स्कूल्स ऑफ राजस्थान मामले (2012) में सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने RTE अधिनियम और निजी गैर-अल्पसंख्यक विद्यालयों में 25 प्रतिशत प्रवेश प्रावधान की संवैधानिक वैधता को बरकरार रखा। न्यायालय ने इसे अनुच्छेद 19(6) के संदर्भ में सार्वजनिक हित का उचित प्रतिबंध माना। तीसरा कथन गलत है, क्योंकि बाद के Pramati Educational and Cultural Trust निर्णय में अनुच्छेद 30(1) के अल्पसंख्यक संस्थानों को RTE अधिनियम के इस दायरे से बाहर रखा गया।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) I and II

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: In Society for Unaided Private Schools of Rajasthan (2012), the Supreme Court upheld the RTE Act and validated 25% reservations in private non-minority schools as reasonable restrictions under Article 19(6). Statement III is incorrect because the Court exempted minority institutions from the RTE Act's purview.

questions.question_english: Which schedule of the Constitution deals with the allocation of powers and functions between the Union and the States, significantly impacting educational administration?
options_english: Fifth Schedule
Sixth Schedule
Seventh Schedule
Ninth Schedule
questions.explanation_english: The Seventh Schedule distributes legislative subjects between the Union and States across three lists: List I (Union List), List II (State List), and List III (Concurrent List). Entry 25 of the Concurrent List governs education, serving as the constitutional framework dividing legislative powers in educational administration.

key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) Seventh Schedule

questions.question_english:
Consider these statements regarding the Unni Krishnan judgment (1993):
I. It explicitly separated the right to elementary education from the right to higher education.
II. It declared that higher education is not a fundamental right.
III. It established the scheme for regulating admissions and fee structures in private professional colleges.

questions.explanation_english: In Unni Krishnan (1993), the Supreme Court separated elementary education (a fundamental right up to age 14) from higher education (which is subject to economic capacity). The Court created a detailed regulatory scheme for professional college admissions and fee structures to curb commercialization, making all three statements correct.

Assertion (A): The Fundamental Right to Education (Article 21A) is self-executing and did not require any legislation to be implemented.

Consider the following Assertion (A) and Reason (R).
Assertion (A): The Right to Education under Article 21A cannot be suspended during a National Emergency.
Reason (R): Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended during a National Emergency, and Article 21A, being a corollary to Article 21, enjoys the same protection.
options_english: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false

questions.explanation_english: The 44th Amendment ensured Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended during Emergency under Article 359. Since Article 21A was derived from and inserted directly after Article 21, its enforcement remains non-suspendable during a National Emergency, making the reason a correct explanation.
